newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS - Speculation rampant on Intel.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS - Speculation rampant on Intel.

text.p: Intel Corp options traded heavily at the American Stock Exchange Wednesday as the stock fell sharply on huge volume after the company reported quarterly earnings.
Traders said put and call buying was the main thrust of investors, with some investors buying January calls hoping for a quick pop in the stock by Friday.
"We've got a lot of people buying the January 145 call just looking for a pop in the stock," a broker on the East Coast said. "We're getting a lot of short-term speculators."
Traders said other investors were buying puts, convinced that the stock has seen a near-term top and is beginning a correction.
In late trading, shares of the chip maker were down 4-7/8 at 142-1/4 on turnover of more than 28 million shares.
On Tuesday, the stock closed at 147-1/8, an all-time closing high. It had reached a record intraday peak of 149-3/4.
After the market close Tuesday, Intel reported fourth quarter profits of $2.13 per share, more than double from a year earlier and better than Wall Street's consensus.
But concern over projected flat first quarter revenues and the fact that the results were shy of some expectations pushed the stock lower Wednesday.

"With all the speculation around the earnings, we had a lot of call and put buyers, mostly on the call side betting the earnings were going to be better than expected," said Ken Walker at EVEREN Securities in Chicago.

"The one thing they didn't quite understand, even if the stock didn't bounce higher, was that with premiums being as high as they were, the odds of really making any money were going to be pretty thin," he said.
He added that call premiums then got crushed as the stock failed to rally and instead moved sharply lower.

In late trading the Intel January 145 call was the most active in the group, with about 15,300 contracts changing hands. The option, which had open interest of 17,483 contracts through Tuesday, was down 4-3/8 at one.
The January 150 call, with volume of 11,300 contracts and open interest of 21,244, fell 2-7/8 to 1/4.
Among the Intel puts, the most active was the January 145, which traded 8,455. Its open interest was 5,822 and it rose 3/8 to 3-5/8.
"We're getting a lot of volatility players on it," the broker on the East Coast said. "People are liking the fact that they're splitting two-for-one and all the rest of it."
Along with its earnings release Tuesday, Intel announced a two-for-one stock split.
